description:
/fly HUD speed readout shows 'NaN km/s' for outer-planet missions (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto) throughout the interplanetary cruise phase

Expected: The HUD speed readout should show a numeric km/s value for every mission, including outer-planet destinations, for every position along the trajectory

Acceptance criteria:
- heliocentricSpeed(rAu, aTransferAu) must not return NaN for any rAu > 0, aTransferAu > 0 [code-invariant: NaN in a speed computation is a crash-level defect — no document needed]
- When the vis-viva radicand (2/rAu - 1/aTransferAu) is negative (i.e., rAu >= 2 * aTransferAu), heliocentricSpeed falls back to the local circular orbital speed sqrt(mu / rAu) [reporter: Reporter answer: 'It should fall back to the local circular orbital speed at that radius, sqrt(mu / r)']
- The /fly HUD displays a non-NaN numeric km/s value for every outer-planet mission catalog entry (Galileo, Voyager 2, New Horizons, Dawn) across the full trajectory time range [reporter: Bug report: 'the HUD speed readout just says NaN km/s the whole way']

Domain facts:
- static/data/planets.json: Earth a=1.0 AU, Mars a=1.52366 AU → (1+1.52366)/2 = 1.26183 AU is the hardcoded aTransfer for all non-Moon missions
- The e2e validation test (tests/e2e/fly-render-validation.spec.ts:115-117) has its own local visViva function duplicating the NaN-vulnerable formula; it only exercises Moon and Mars cases, so the bug is invisible to CI
